questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses inversion to emphasize the adverbial phrase.

A. Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
B. Only after the storm passed did the children go out to play.
C. So fast did the car go that it almost crashed.
D. Hardly had she arrived when the meeting started.
options: Never before have I seen such a beautiful sunset.
Only after the storm passed did the children go out to play.
So fast did the car go that it almost crashed.
Hardly had she arrived when the meeting started.
questions.answer: Only after the storm passed did the children go out to play.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly employs a cleft sentence to highlight the specific detail about the discovery?

A. It was in the old library that the historian found the rare manuscript.
B. The rare manuscript was found by the historian in the old library.
C. The historian found the rare manuscript, but not in the old library.
D. The rare manuscript, discovered in the old library, was found by the historian.
options: It was in the old library that the historian found the rare manuscript.
The rare manuscript was found by the historian in the old library.
The historian found the rare manuscript, but not in the old library.
The rare manuscript, discovered in the old library, was found by the historian.
questions.answer: It was in the old library that the historian found the rare manuscript.

questions.question:
Select the option that correctly uses the third conditional to express a hypothetical situation in the past that did not happen.

A. If I had known about the concert, I would have gone.
B. If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
C. If I had been you, I would have taken the job.
D. If I had known the address, I should have written to them by now.
options: If I had known about the concert, I would have gone.
If I had studied harder, I would have passed the exam.
If I had been you, I would have taken the job.
If I had known the address, I should have written to them by now.
questions.answer: If I had known the address, I should have written to them by now.

questions.question:
Which sentence correctly uses the subjunctive mood to express a formal recommendation or requirement?

A. I suggest that he leaves immediately.
B. It is recommended that the measures be implemented without delay.
C. We advise that she consults a specialist.
D. They demand that the contract be signed by tomorrow.
options: I suggest that he leaves immediately.
It is recommended that the measures be implemented without delay.
We advise that she consults a specialist.
They demand that the contract be signed by tomorrow.
questions.answer: It is recommended that the measures be implemented without delay.

questions.question:
Identify the sentence that correctly uses ellipsis to omit an understood word or phrase, maintaining grammatical coherence.

A. She enjoys painting, and so does her brother.
B. He speaks English, and she too.
C. We went to the cinema, and they did too.
D. They finished the project, and so they did.
options: She enjoys painting, and so does her brother.
He speaks English, and she too.
We went to the cinema, and they did too.
They finished the project, and so they did.
questions.answer: She enjoys painting, and so does her brother.
